chapters.1.summary: Jacob’s seventy descendants in Egypt grow into a great people after Joseph dies. A new king who did not know Joseph fears their numbers. He sets taskmasters over them, and they build the store cities Pithom and Raamses. The harder Egypt presses them, the more they multiply. The king tells the Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah, to kill newborn boys. The midwives fear God and let the boys live. God deals well with them and gives them families. Pharaoh then orders all his people to throw Hebrew baby boys into the river.
chapters.1.lds: The midwives “feared God” and disobeyed the king (verse 17). What did Pharaoh fear in verses 9–10?
chapters.2.summary: A Levite woman bears a son and hides him three months. She puts him in a papyrus basket among the river reeds, and his sister watches. Pharaoh’s daughter finds him, pities him, and knows he is a Hebrew child. The sister offers a nurse and brings the boy’s own mother. Pharaoh’s daughter adopts him and names him Moses. Grown, Moses kills an Egyptian who beat a Hebrew, and he flees to Midian. He defends seven sisters at a well and marries one, Zipporah. Israel groans in slavery, and God hears and remembers his covenant.
chapters.2.lds: Moses 1 expands Moses’s later encounter with God. Keep that account distinct from his childhood. Three women save the child in verses 2–10. Who are they?
chapters.3.summary: Moses keeps his father-in-law’s flock and comes to Horeb, God’s mountain. He sees a bush on fire that does not burn up. God calls him by name and tells him to take off his sandals. The LORD has seen his people’s suffering and has come down to rescue them. He sends Moses to Pharaoh, and Moses asks, “Who am I?” God promises to be with him and gives his name: “I AM WHO I AM.” Moses must tell the elders and then ask Pharaoh for a three-day journey. God says Pharaoh will refuse until God strikes Egypt.
chapters.3.lds: The Church manual reads Moses’s call as preparation for prophetic service. The LORD says, “I know their sorrows” (verse 7). What does he say he has come down to do in verse 8?
chapters.4.summary: Moses says the people will not believe him. The LORD gives him three signs with a rod, his hand, and river water. Moses says he is slow of speech and asks God to send someone else. The LORD is angry and names Aaron, his brother, to speak for him. Moses takes leave of Jethro and sets out with his wife and sons. The LORD tells him to call Israel “my firstborn” before Pharaoh. On the way the LORD meets him to kill him, and Zipporah circumcises her son. Aaron meets Moses, and the people believe and worship.
chapters.4.lds: Moses asks the Lord to send someone else (verse 13). Whom does the LORD send with him in verses 14–16?
chapters.5.summary: Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh the LORD’s word: let my people go. Pharaoh says he does not know the LORD and will not let Israel go. He calls the people idle. That day he orders that they get no straw but make as many bricks. The people scatter to gather stubble, and their Israelite officers are beaten. The officers appeal to Pharaoh, and he repeats, “You are idle!” They blame Moses and Aaron. Moses asks the LORD why he sent him, since the people are not rescued.
chapters.5.lds: Things get worse after Moses obeys. What does Moses say to the LORD in verses 22–23?
chapters.6.summary: The LORD tells Moses that Pharaoh will drive Israel out by a strong hand. God says he is the LORD, who made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. He has heard Israel groan and remembers that covenant. He promises to free them, take them as his people, and give them the land. The people do not listen, because of crushed spirits and cruel slavery. Moses asks how Pharaoh will listen if Israel will not. The chapter lists the families of Reuben, Simeon, and Levi, down to Aaron and Moses. The LORD again sends Moses to Pharaoh.
chapters.6.lds: The covenant promise includes belonging to God. The people cannot listen to Moses (verse 9). What two reasons does the verse give?
chapters.7.summary: The LORD makes Moses like God to Pharaoh, with Aaron as his prophet. He says Pharaoh will not listen, and Egypt will learn that he is the LORD. Moses is eighty and Aaron eighty-three. Aaron’s rod becomes a serpent before Pharaoh, and it swallows the magicians’ rods. Pharaoh’s heart stays hard. In the morning Aaron strikes the river, and its water turns to blood. The fish die, and the Egyptians dig for water to drink. The magicians do the same, and Pharaoh goes home unmoved.
chapters.7.lds: Pharaoh goes into his house and does not take it to heart (verse 23). What must ordinary Egyptians do in verse 24?
chapters.8.summary: Frogs come up from the river and fill houses, beds, and ovens. Pharaoh asks Moses to pray and promises to let the people go. The frogs die, and Pharaoh hardens his heart. Aaron strikes the dust, and it becomes lice on people and animals. The magicians cannot copy it and say, “This is God’s finger.” Swarms of flies fill Egypt, but not Goshen, where Israel lives. Pharaoh offers a sacrifice inside Egypt, then a short trip into the wilderness. Moses prays, the flies leave, and Pharaoh again refuses.
chapters.8.lds: Pharaoh says Israel may go, “only you shall not go very far away” (verse 28). What happens to his promise in verse 32?
chapters.9.summary: A disease kills Egypt’s livestock in the field, but none of Israel’s animals die. Moses throws furnace ashes into the air, and boils break out on people and animals. The magicians cannot stand before Moses. The LORD says he let Pharaoh stand to show his power in all the earth. He warns of heavy hail and tells Egypt to bring servants and animals inside. Some of Pharaoh’s servants fear the word and obey; others do not. Hail and fire strike all Egypt except Goshen. Pharaoh says he has sinned, but when the hail stops he hardens his heart.
chapters.9.lds: Pharaoh says, “I have sinned this time” (verse 27). What does verse 34 say he did when the hail stopped?
chapters.10.summary: The LORD says these signs are for Israel to tell their children and grandchildren. Moses warns of locusts, and Pharaoh’s servants beg him to let the men go. Pharaoh asks who will go, and Moses says everyone, with flocks and herds. Pharaoh will let only the men go and drives Moses out. Locusts eat every green thing the hail left. Pharaoh admits sin, the locusts are blown into the Red Sea, and he refuses again. Three days of thick darkness cover Egypt, but Israel has light. Pharaoh says to go but leave the animals, and Moses says not a hoof stays.
chapters.10.lds: Pharaoh will let the people go if the flocks stay (verse 24). Why does Moses say every animal must come in verse 26?
chapters.11.summary: The LORD tells Moses that one more plague will make Pharaoh drive Israel out. The people are to ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver and gold. Moses is highly regarded in Egypt. He tells Pharaoh the LORD will go through Egypt about midnight. Every firstborn will die, from Pharaoh’s son to the slave girl’s at the mill. A great cry will rise, but not a dog will bark at Israel. Moses leaves Pharaoh in hot anger. The LORD hardens Pharaoh’s heart, and he still refuses.
chapters.11.lds: The plague reaches from the throne to the slave at the mill (verse 5). How do these deaths affect your reading of Israel’s freedom?
chapters.12.summary: The LORD makes this month the first of the year. Each household must take a lamb without defect and kill it on the fourteenth day. They put its blood on the door posts and eat it roasted, dressed to leave. The LORD will strike Egypt’s firstborn and pass over the houses with blood. Israel must keep this day and seven days of bread without yeast, forever. At midnight every Egyptian house has someone dead, and Pharaoh tells Israel to go. They leave in haste with unrisen dough and Egyptian silver and gold. About 600,000 men leave on foot, with a mixed crowd, after 430 years.
chapters.12.lds: The Church manual connects the Passover lamb with Jesus Christ. Children will ask what the Passover service means (verse 26). What answer does verse 27 give?
chapters.13.summary: The LORD claims every firstborn male in Israel, human and animal. Moses tells the people to remember this day with seven days of unleavened bread. They must tell their sons what the LORD did when they left Egypt. Firstborn animals are sacrificed, and firstborn sons are bought back. God does not lead them by the near road through Philistine land. He says they might see war and return to Egypt. He leads them by the wilderness toward the Red Sea, and Moses carries Joseph’s bones. The LORD goes ahead in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
chapters.13.lds: God chose the longer road (verses 17–18). What reason does verse 17 give?
chapters.14.summary: The LORD has Israel camp by the sea, so Pharaoh will think they are trapped. Pharaoh regrets freeing his slaves and chases them with six hundred chosen chariots. The people see the army, cry out, and tell Moses that serving Egypt was better. Moses says to stand still and see the LORD’s rescue. The cloud moves behind Israel, between the two camps. Moses stretches out his hand, and an east wind divides the sea all night. Israel crosses on dry ground with walls of water on each side. The Egyptians follow, the water returns, and not one of them is left.
chapters.14.lds: First Nephi 17 recalls the sea crossing to teach trust in God. The people say serving Egypt was better (verse 12). What does Moses tell them to do in verses 13–14?
chapters.15.summary: Moses and Israel sing to the LORD, who threw horse and rider into the sea. The song says the LORD is a warrior, and Pharaoh’s captains sank like a stone. It says the nations tremble and the LORD will plant his people on his mountain. Miriam the prophetess leads the women with tambourines and dancing. Israel then walks three days in the wilderness without water. At Marah the water is bitter, and the people grumble at Moses. The LORD shows Moses a tree that makes the water sweet. He promises health if they listen, and they camp at Elim’s twelve springs.
chapters.15.lds: Three days after the song, the people ask Moses what they will drink (verse 24). What does the LORD call himself in verse 26?
chapters.16.summary: In the second month Israel reaches the wilderness of Sin and complains of hunger. They say they wish they had died by the meat pots of Egypt. The LORD promises bread from the sky each day, as a test. Quail come at evening, and a fine flake covers the ground at dawn. Each person gathers an omer, and no one has too much or too little. What is kept overnight rots, except on the sixth day, when they gather double. On the seventh day there is none, because it is the Sabbath. They call it manna and eat it forty years.
chapters.16.lds: The Church manual connects manna with reliance on God. Some gathered more and some less (verse 17). What does verse 18 say each one ended with?
chapters.17.summary: Israel camps at Rephidim, where there is no water. The people quarrel with Moses and say he brought them out to die. Moses cries to the LORD and says they are ready to stone him. He strikes the rock at Horeb before the elders, and water comes out. The place is named Massah and Meribah for their testing and quarrel. Amalek attacks, and Joshua leads the fight while Moses stands on the hill. Israel wins while Moses’ hands are up, so Aaron and Hur hold them until sunset. Moses builds an altar named “The LORD our Banner.”
chapters.17.lds: Moses cannot keep his hands up alone (verse 12). Who helps him, and how?
chapters.18.summary: Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law and priest of Midian, hears what the LORD did for Israel. He brings Moses’ wife Zipporah and their two sons to the camp. Moses tells him everything, and Jethro blesses the LORD and offers sacrifices. The next day Moses judges the people alone from morning to evening. Jethro says this is not good and will wear out Moses and the people. He advises choosing honest, able men to judge small cases. Hard cases will still come to Moses. Moses does all this, and Jethro goes home.
chapters.18.lds: Jethro tells Moses, “The thing that you do is not good” (verse 17). Who gains from his plan in verse 23?
chapters.19.summary: In the third month Israel camps before Mount Sinai. The LORD reminds them how he carried them on eagles’ wings. If they keep his covenant, they will be his own, a kingdom of priests. All the people answer that they will do what the LORD has spoken. They wash their clothes, and a boundary is set around the mountain. On the third day there is thunder, lightning, thick cloud, and a loud trumpet. The mountain smokes and shakes as the LORD comes down in fire. Moses goes up and is sent back to warn the people.
chapters.19.lds: The Church manual connects covenant belonging with duties of holiness and service. The people answer together in verse 8. What had God done for them before he asked (verse 4)?
chapters.20.summary: God speaks and names himself as the one who brought Israel out of slavery. He commands no other gods, no idols, and no misuse of his name. The seventh day is a Sabbath of rest for children, servants, animals, and strangers. They must honor father and mother. They must not murder, commit adultery, steal, give false testimony, or covet. The people tremble at the thunder and smoke and stand far off. They ask Moses to speak for God, and Moses goes into the thick darkness. The LORD forbids gods of silver or gold and allows a plain altar of earth.
chapters.20.lds: The Church manual studies how each command can shape faithful choices. The Sabbath command names who must rest (verse 10). Who is on the list besides the head of the house?
chapters.21.summary: These are the rulings set before Israel. A Hebrew servant serves six years and goes free in the seventh. A daughter sold as a servant keeps rights to food and clothing, or goes free. Murder brings death, but an accidental killer may flee to a set place. Kidnapping and striking or cursing parents bring death. One who injures another pays for lost time and healing. A master who destroys a servant’s eye or tooth must free that servant. Owners pay for harm from an open pit or a bull known to gore.
chapters.21.lds: These laws come from an ancient legal setting. A servant who loses an eye goes free (verse 26). What does verse 21 show about the servant’s standing?
chapters.22.summary: A thief pays back more than he stole, up to five oxen for one. A person pays for crops ruined by his animal or his fire. Disputes over goods left in another’s care come before God. A man who seduces an unpledged virgin must pay a dowry for her. Israel must not wrong a foreigner, because they were foreigners in Egypt. God will hear the cry of any widow or fatherless child they wrong. Lenders must not charge the poor interest. A cloak taken as a pledge must be returned before sunset.
chapters.22.lds: A poor borrower’s cloak must be returned by sunset (verse 26). What reason does verse 27 give?
chapters.23.summary: Israel must not spread false reports or follow a crowd to do evil. Judges must not favor the poor or deny them justice, and must refuse bribes. A person must return an enemy’s stray ox and help his fallen donkey. Israel must not oppress foreigners, since they know a foreigner’s heart. The land rests every seventh year so the poor may eat. The seventh day gives rest to animals, servants, and foreigners. Three feasts are kept each year. God will send an angel ahead and drive out the nations little by little.
chapters.23.lds: The law tells Israel to help the donkey of “him who hates you” (verse 5). What does the helper have to set aside?
chapters.24.summary: The LORD calls Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders to come up and worship. Moses tells the people all the LORD’s words, and they promise to do them. He writes the words down and builds an altar with twelve pillars. He reads the book of the covenant aloud, and the people again promise to obey. Moses sprinkles blood on the altar and on the people. The leaders go up, see the God of Israel, and eat and drink. The LORD calls Moses higher to receive stone tablets. Moses enters the cloud and stays forty days and nights.
chapters.24.lds: A covenant includes an informed promise. The people promise after hearing the book read (verse 7). What did they promise before, in verse 3?
chapters.25.summary: The LORD tells Moses to take an offering from everyone with a willing heart. The gifts are gold, silver, bronze, fine cloth, skins, wood, oil, spices, and stones. The people are to make a sanctuary so that God may live among them. They must follow the pattern God shows Moses. The ark is a gold-covered chest with poles, and it holds the covenant. Its gold cover, the mercy seat, has two cherubim, and God will meet Moses there. A gold-covered table holds the bread of the presence. A lamp stand of pure gold has seven lamps.
chapters.25.lds: The Church manual connects the tabernacle with worship and God’s presence among His people. God gives the reason for the sanctuary in verse 8. What is it?
chapters.26.summary: The tabernacle is made of ten linen curtains in blue, purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. Gold clasps join them into one piece. A cover of goats’ hair goes over it, then ram skins and hides. Upright boards of acacia wood stand in silver sockets and are held by bars. All of it follows what Moses saw on the mountain. A veil with cherubim hangs on four pillars inside. The ark goes behind the veil, in the most holy place. The table and lamp stand stay outside the veil, and a screen covers the door.
chapters.26.lds: The veil separates the holy place from the most holy (verse 33). What is placed behind it?
chapters.27.summary: The altar is square, made of acacia wood covered with bronze, with horns. Its pots, shovels, basins, and grating are bronze, and poles carry it. The court around the tabernacle is one hundred cubits long and fifty wide. Linen hangings on bronze-footed pillars form its walls. A screen of blue, purple, and scarlet covers the gate. The people of Israel must bring pure beaten olive oil for the lamp. Aaron and his sons keep the lamp burning from evening to morning. This is a lasting rule for Israel.
chapters.27.lds: The lamp must burn “continually” (verse 20). Who supplies the oil, and who tends the lamp?
chapters.28.summary: Aaron and his four sons become priests, and skilled workers make Aaron’s holy garments. The ephod, a priestly garment, has two shoulder stones with the names of Israel’s sons. The breastplate holds twelve stones, one for each tribe. Aaron carries the names over his heart when he enters the holy place. The Urim and Thummim go in the breastplate. A blue robe has gold bells on its hem. A gold plate on his forehead says “HOLY TO THE LORD.” His sons receive tunics, sashes, and headbands.
chapters.28.lds: Aaron carries Israel’s names on his shoulders and over his heart (verses 12 and 29). For whom does he go into the holy place?
chapters.29.summary: Moses is told how to make Aaron and his sons priests. They are washed, dressed in the holy garments, and anointed with oil. A bull is offered for sin, and a ram is burned whole. Blood from a second ram goes on each priest’s right ear, thumb, and big toe. The priests eat their share of that ram at the tent door. The rites last seven days and also make the altar holy. After that two lambs are offered every day, one at morning and one at evening. God says he will meet Israel there and live among them.
chapters.29.lds: The Church manual studies preparation for sacred service. After seven days of rites, God states his aim in verses 45–46. What is it?
chapters.30.summary: A small gold altar for incense stands before the veil. Aaron burns incense on it every morning and evening. When Israel is counted, each man twenty and older gives half a shekel. The rich give no more and the poor no less. The money serves the Tent of Meeting. A bronze basin holds water for the priests to wash hands and feet. A holy spiced oil anoints the tent, its furniture, and the priests. No one may copy the oil or the incense for private use.
chapters.30.lds: Rich and poor pay the same half shekel (verse 15). What does the verse say the payment is for?
chapters.31.summary: The LORD names Bezalel of Judah and fills him with God’s Spirit and skill. He will work in gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood. Oholiab of Dan will work with him, and other skilled people will help. They are to make the tent, its furniture, the garments, the oil, and the incense. Then the LORD says Israel must surely keep his Sabbaths. The Sabbath is a sign between God and Israel for all generations. Six days are for work, and the seventh is holy rest. God gives Moses two stone tablets written with his finger.
chapters.31.lds: Right after naming the builders, God commands the Sabbath (verse 13). Why might the two be placed together?
chapters.32.summary: Moses delays on the mountain, and the people ask Aaron to make gods. Aaron collects their gold earrings and makes a calf. The people say these gods brought them out of Egypt, and they feast. The LORD tells Moses he will destroy them, and Moses pleads for them. The LORD turns from the harm he spoke of. Moses comes down, sees the calf and dancing, and breaks the tablets. He grinds the calf to powder, and Aaron blames the people and the fire. The Levites kill about three thousand, and Moses asks God to forgive the people.
chapters.32.lds: The people call the calf the gods who brought them out of Egypt (verse 4). Whom had they just promised to obey in 24:7?
chapters.33.summary: The LORD tells Moses to lead the people on, with an angel ahead. He says he will not go among them, because they are stubborn. The people mourn and take off their jewelry. Moses pitches a tent outside the camp, and the cloud comes down when he enters. The LORD speaks with Moses face to face, as with a friend. Moses says that if God’s presence does not go, they should not leave. The LORD agrees to go with them. Moses asks to see God’s glory and is allowed to see his back.
chapters.33.lds: God offers the land with an angel but without himself (verses 2–3). What does Moses say in verse 15?
chapters.34.summary: Moses cuts two new stone tablets and goes up Sinai alone. The LORD comes down in the cloud and declares his name. He is merciful, slow to anger, and forgiving, yet does not clear the guilty. Moses bows and asks God to go with this stubborn people and pardon them. The LORD makes a covenant and promises wonders. Israel must make no treaty with the people of the land or worship their gods. The feasts, firstborn, and Sabbath laws are repeated. Moses comes down with a shining face and afterward wears a veil.
chapters.34.lds: The Church manual reads renewal alongside repentance. The LORD describes himself after the calf (verses 6–7). Which words come first?
chapters.35.summary: Moses gathers all Israel and repeats the Sabbath rule first. Then he asks for an offering from everyone with a willing heart. He lists what must be made, from the tent to the priests’ garments. Men and women bring gold jewelry, cloth, skins, silver, bronze, and wood. Skilled women spin the colored yarn and the goats’ hair. The rulers bring stones, spice, and oil. All of it is a free offering to the LORD. Moses names Bezalel and Oholiab, whom God filled with skill to work and teach.
chapters.35.lds: Men and women bring gifts because their hearts are willing (verse 29). How does this work differ from the brick making in chapter 5?
chapters.36.summary: Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker begin the work. The people keep bringing free gifts every morning. The workers tell Moses there is far more than enough. Moses orders that no one bring anything more, and the people stop. The workers make the ten linen curtains with cherubim and join them with gold clasps. They make the goats’ hair covering and the skin coverings. They set up acacia boards in silver sockets and overlay them with gold. They make the veil and the screen for the door.
chapters.36.lds: The people give so much that Moses tells them to stop (verse 6). What does that say about the purpose of the collection?
chapters.37.summary: Bezalel makes the ark of acacia wood and covers it with gold inside and out. He makes its rings and poles for carrying. He makes the gold mercy seat with two cherubim facing each other. He makes the gold-covered table and its dishes. He makes the lamp stand from one piece of pure gold, with seven lamps. He makes the gold incense altar with its poles. He makes the holy oil and the incense.
chapters.37.lds: Bezalel makes the ark as 25:10–11 described (verses 1–2). Why might the book repeat each detail?
chapters.38.summary: Bezalel makes the bronze altar for burnt offerings with its tools and poles. He makes the bronze basin from the mirrors of women serving at the tent. He makes the court with linen hangings, bronze sockets, and silver hooks. Then the chapter gives the amounts of the materials. Ithamar, Aaron’s son, kept the count for the Levites. The gold weighed over twenty-nine talents. The silver came from the half shekel paid by 603,550 men. The bronze weighed over seventy talents, and each metal’s use is listed.
chapters.38.lds: The chapter lists how much gold, silver, and bronze was used (verses 24–31). Who kept the count, according to verse 21?
chapters.39.summary: The workers make Aaron’s holy garments from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. They beat gold into thin wires and weave it into the ephod. They set the onyx shoulder stones and the twelve stones of the breastplate. They make the blue robe with bells and pomegranates on its hem. They make tunics, turbans, and sashes, and the gold plate reading “HOLY TO THE LORD.” All the work is finished as the LORD commanded Moses. The people bring every part to Moses. He inspects it and blesses them.
chapters.39.lds: Moses looks over all the work before he blesses the people (verse 43). What did he find?
chapters.40.summary: The LORD tells Moses to raise the tabernacle on the year’s first day. Moses puts the covenant in the ark and hangs the veil in front of it. He sets the table, the lamp stand, and the incense altar in their places. He puts the altar of burnt offering and the basin outside. He anoints the tent and washes and dresses Aaron and his sons. Moses finishes the work, and the cloud covers the tent. The LORD’s glory fills it, and Moses cannot enter. Israel travels when the cloud lifts and stays when it rests.
chapters.40.lds: The Church manual connects the sanctuary with God’s presence. The cloud fills the tent and also leads the journey (verses 34–38). What do the people do when it lifts?
